headline: The investment bank Panmure Liberum forecasts that the S&P 500 will fall to 5,000 by the end of 2027, and says the stock market's long rise may be nearing its end.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: a bold forecast from one investment bank, reported briefly by Reuters, with only the broad reason given.
importance_line: People who hold US share funds would face large losses if the forecast came true, but it is one firm's prediction and the short report gives only rising bond yields and interest rates as its reason.
summary: Reuters reports that Panmure Liberum expects the S&P 500, the index of 500 large US companies, to fall to 5,000 points by the end of 2027, warning in a Monday note that the market's resilience could unravel if bond yields and interest rates keep rising. "We think the end of the equity bull market may be closer than many investors think," Panmure said; the index closed Monday at 7,773.95, so the forecast implies a fall of about 36% (our calculation).
